idea-plugin.name: Order Annotation Sorting
idea-plugin.description:
Sorts classes in the Project view by their @Order(n) annotation, so the order of the files in a package matches the order your code runs in. This is useful for things like filters, interceptors, migrations, pipeline steps and configuration classes.

How classes are ordered

  • No annotated classes in a package: the package keeps the IDE's default ordering.
  • At least one annotated class: annotated classes come first, by ascending value. Classes with equal values are sorted by name.
  • Non-annotated classes and other files follow, sorted by name.
  • Subpackages keep their usual position.

Supported annotations and values

  • Any annotation with the simple name Order works, for example Spring's org.springframework.core.annotation.Order or your own.
  • Values can be literals (@Order(1), @Order(value = -5)) or constant expressions (@Order(Ordered.HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE + 1)).
  • @Order without a value is treated as Integer.MAX_VALUE, matching Spring.

The view updates as you edit annotations. Ordering applies to the Sort by Name and Sort by Type modes. Sort by Modification Time and manual ordering take precedence when selected.
